title: Landfill for household waste
prompt: The diagrams show how a modern landfill for household waste is built, used and finally closed. Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant. Write at least 150 words.

paragraphs.introduction: The diagrams show how a modern landfill for household waste is built, used and finally closed.
paragraphs.overview: Overall, the landfill is a man-made hole with protective layers and a drainage system. Waste is placed inside the hole, which is covered with clay when it is full, while gases can leave through a pipe.
paragraphs.body1: First, a large hole is dug in natural rock. A layer of clay is placed along its sides and bottom, and a synthetic substance is added as another protective layer. Drainage pipes are then installed at the bottom of the hole. These pipes are connected to a drainage tank, forming the system needed before the landfill can be used.
paragraphs.body2: During use, household waste is put into the prepared hole. Liquid from the waste collects towards the bottom, where the drainage system is located. Once the landfill has reached the closure stage, the waste is covered with a layer of clay. The waste remains below this cover, and gases are able to pass out through the pipe shown on the right-hand side.

paragraphs.introduction: The diagram shows the main parts of a central heating system in a house and how the system operates.
paragraphs.overview: Overall, the system uses a boiler and a pump to send hot water around the house. It includes a storage tank, pipes and several radiators, and it also provides hot water for the taps.
paragraphs.body1: Cold water enters the house through a pipe near the roof. A small water tank is located at the top of the building to fill the storage tank below it. An overflow pipe is also shown beside this upper part of the system. The storage tank is connected to the boiler, which is placed lower down in the house and is powered by either gas or oil.
paragraphs.body2: The boiler heats the water, and the pump moves hot water through the pipes to the radiators. These radiators are positioned in different parts of the house and are connected by small tubes. After passing through the heating circuit, cooler water returns towards the boiler to be heated again. A separate connection from the storage tank supplies hot water to the household taps.

title: New Zealand kiwi fruit exports
prompt: The table compares the value of New Zealand kiwi fruit exports to five countries in 2010, 2011 and 2012, measured in New Zealand dollars. Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant. Write at least 150 words.
source_label: Ngân hàng đề người dùng cung cấp

paragraphs.introduction: The table compares the value of New Zealand kiwi fruit exports to five countries in 2010, 2011 and 2012, measured in New Zealand dollars.
paragraphs.overview: Overall, Japan was by far the largest market in all three years, followed by China. Export values increased in these two countries and Russia, whereas the figures for Mexico and Saudi Arabia ended below their starting levels.
paragraphs.body1: Exports to Japan were worth $271.1 million in 2010, after which they rose to $287.4 million in 2011 and $325.3 million in 2012. A similar increase was seen in China, where the value went from $74.9 million to $84.8 million before reaching $94 million. These two markets were much larger than the other three throughout the period.
paragraphs.body2: In contrast, the value for Mexico fell from $6 million to $2.4 million, before recovering to $3.3 million in 2012. Russia recorded steady growth across the three figures, from $968,000 to $1.585 million and then $2.404 million. Saudi Arabia remained the smallest market: exports initially rose from $290,000 to $407,000, but then dropped sharply to just $82,000.

This finished material can then be taken out and used in the garden.

paragraphs.overview: Overall, the town gained more tourist facilities, while farmland and some coastal facilities were removed. The golf course and the main road layout remained, but the coastline was used differently by the end of the period.

paragraphs.introduction: The diagram shows how rainwater is collected and treated so that it can be used as drinking water in an Australian town.
paragraphs.overview: Overall, rainwater is gathered from the roofs of houses and passes through a filter and two tanks. After chemical treatment, the water is sent back to the houses for people to drink.
paragraphs.body1: At the beginning of the process, rain falls onto the roofs of the houses. It runs down through drains attached to the buildings and enters an underground pipe. This pipe connects the houses to a water filter. The collected rainwater passes through the filter before flowing into a storage tank, where it is kept ahead of the next treatment stage.
paragraphs.body2: Water then leaves the storage tank through another pipe and enters a separate water treatment tank. Chemicals are added at this stage, as shown by the small container above the tank. Once treatment is complete, the water flows along a supply pipe leading back towards the houses. It is carried upwards into each building, where it comes out of the taps as drinking water.

paragraphs.introduction: The diagram shows the stages involved in manufacturing ceramic pots, from obtaining raw materials to producing the finished items.
paragraphs.overview: Overall, the process includes preparing and shaping the material, followed by drying, heating and colouring. The pots are heated twice, with colour being added between the two heating stages.
paragraphs.body1: First, raw materials are dug out of the ground using a machine. They are loaded onto a truck and transported to the factory. paragraphs.body2: Next, the assembled pots are put into an oven and heated at 1,000 degrees Celsius. After this stage, they are dipped into colour, as shown by a pot being lowered into a container. The coloured pots then undergo another heating stage, labelled colour firing in the diagram. At the end of this final stage, the ceramic pots are complete and ready as finished products.

paragraphs.overview: Overall, all three countries exported more coffee at the end than at the beginning. Brazil became the largest exporter, while Colombia showed the sharpest fluctuations and remained below the other two countries in 2012.
paragraphs.body1: Brazil exported approximately 12 million kilograms in 2002. Its figure rose to about 15 million in 2006 and 20 million in 2008, before slipping to around 18 million in 2010. They subsequently recovered, reaching 20 million in the final year.

paragraphs.introduction: The table compares the average weekly salaries of men and women in five occupational groups in 2015, measured in dollars.
paragraphs.overview: Overall, men earned more than women in every occupation. Professionals received the highest salaries for both sexes, while manual workers earned the least. The largest gap between men and women was among technicians.
paragraphs.body1: Male professionals earned $2,000 per week, compared with $1,900 for female professionals. This difference of $100 was the smallest gap in the table. Technicians showed a much larger difference: the average for men was $1,400, whereas women received $900. The $500 gap in this group was five times the gap among professionals.
paragraphs.body2: In administrative and clerical work, men earned $1,350 per week and women earned $1,000. Service workers had a similar difference of $350, with weekly salaries of $1,300 for men and $950 for women. Manual workers had the lowest pay in both groups, at $1,100 and $850 respectively. Thus, although the ranking of some occupations differed between men and women, the highest-paid and lowest-paid groups were the same.

paragraphs.overview: Overall, industrial land was replaced by residential, educational and green areas. A harbour and an additional swimming pool were introduced, while several existing features, including the school, convention centre and lake, remained.

title: Underground railways
prompt: The table compares underground railway systems in six cities in terms of opening date, route length and annual passenger numbers. Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant. Write at least 150 words.

paragraphs.introduction: The table compares underground railway systems in six cities in terms of opening date, route length and annual passenger numbers.
paragraphs.overview: Overall, London has the oldest and longest system, while Tokyo carries the most passengers. Kyoto has both the shortest route and the lowest passenger figure, and Los Angeles has the newest system.
paragraphs.body1: London’s railway opened in 1863 and has 394 kilometres of route, almost twice the length of the Paris system at 199 kilometres. Paris opened in 1900 and serves 1,191 million passengers per year, compared with 775 million in London. Tokyo, which opened in 1927, has a shorter route of 155 kilometres but the highest annual passenger total, at 1,927 million.
paragraphs.body2: The remaining systems are smaller and less busy. Washington DC opened in 1976 and has 126 kilometres of route, carrying 144 million passengers annually. Kyoto began operating in 1981 and has only 11 kilometres of route, with 45 million passengers per year. Finally, the Los Angeles system opened in 2001. Its 28-kilometre route is longer than Kyoto’s, but its passenger total is only slightly higher, at 50 million.

title: Renewable power
prompt: The line graph compares the percentage of total energy generated from renewable sources in six countries between 2010 and 2013. Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant. Write at least 150 words.
source_label: Ngân hàng đề người dùng cung cấp
source_note: Đọc từ ảnh gốc. Số ước lượng được ghi about/approximately trong bài.

paragraphs.introduction: The line graph compares the percentage of total energy generated from renewable sources in six countries between 2010 and 2013.
paragraphs.overview: Overall, all six countries ended with higher percentages than they began with. Germany showed the greatest rise and became the leading country, while the USA remained at the bottom of the group throughout the period.
paragraphs.body1: In 2010, China had the highest proportion, at approximately 19%, compared with about 17% in Germany. China’s figure fell to around 17% in 2011, before recovering to just over 20% in 2013. Germany followed a stronger upward trend, increasing to about 20% in 2011 and 25% at the end. India also rose overall, from roughly 17% to around 17.5%, after a small fall in the second year.
paragraphs.body2: The other three countries recorded lower figures. Spain increased gradually from about 13% to approximately 15.5%, while France moved from around 12.5% to 15%. The USA started at roughly 10%, rose to about 12.5% in 2011, and then dipped slightly. By 2013, its proportion had recovered to around 13%, still below those of all the other countries.

analysis_vi: Germany tăng mạnh nhất; USA thấp nhất. Số liệu đường được đọc xấp xỉ, không dùng quiz yêu cầu số thập phân chính xác.

paragraphs.overview: Overall, Australians made up by far the largest share of the population. All five groups were mainly urban, with Chinese residents showing the highest proportion living in cities.
paragraphs.body1: Australians represented 73% of the population, followed by people of other nationalities at 14%. British people were the largest separately identified overseas group, accounting for 7%. Australians had the lowest urban proportion of the five groups, at 80%, and the largest countryside share, at 20%.

title: Carbonated drinks
prompt: The diagram shows the process used to manufacture carbonated drinks, from cleaning water to delivering the finished products to supermarkets. Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant. Write at least 150 words.
source_label: Ngân hàng đề người dùng cung cấp
source_note: Đọc từ ảnh gốc. Số ước lượng được ghi about/approximately trong bài.

paragraphs.introduction: The diagram shows the process used to manufacture carbonated drinks, from cleaning water to delivering the finished products to supermarkets.
paragraphs.overview: Overall, there are five main stages. Water is cleaned, heated and carbonated before other ingredients are mixed in. The drinks are then filtered, placed in containers and packaged for delivery.
paragraphs.body1: In the first stage, raw water passes through a filter and is treated with a water softener and chemicals. A pump then moves the cleaned water to electric heaters. After heating, the water travels through a cooling pipe and enters a tank, where carbon dioxide is added. The resulting carbonated water flows down a pipe to the mixing stage.
paragraphs.body2: Inside the mixing tank, colouring, syrup and flavour are added to the carbonated water. The mixture then passes through another filter before being put into two types of container: bottles and cans. These filled containers are packed into boxes during the final stage. The boxes are loaded onto a truck and transported to a supermarket, completing the process shown in the diagram.

paragraphs.introduction: The bar chart compares the percentages of people with different levels of science qualification in Malaysia and Singapore.
paragraphs.overview: Overall, having no science qualification was the most common situation in both countries. Singapore had a larger proportion of people with a bachelor’s degree, while Malaysia recorded higher shares for school-leaving qualifications and no science qualification.
paragraphs.body1: Approximately 65% of people in Malaysia had no qualification in science, compared with about 60% in Singapore. These were by far the largest figures in the chart. paragraphs.introduction: The maps compare the layout of Forton Valley City in 2000 and 2010.
paragraphs.overview: Overall, farmland and a dairy farm were replaced by public and educational facilities. The area gained a university, a library and a cafe, while the shopping centre and the main roads remained in place.
paragraphs.body1: In 2000, Sheffield Road ran along the northern side, and a second road divided the area into western and eastern sections. The shopping centre occupied the northwest corner. Below it were farmland and a dairy farm. By 2010, the shopping centre was unchanged, but the farmland had become a playground. paragraphs.body1: In 1988, people aged at least 65 accounted for 20% of Germany’s population, compared with 16% in Canada and 14% in the UK. title: Water cycle
prompt: The diagram illustrates the water cycle, showing how water moves between the ocean, the atmosphere and the land. Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant. Write at least 150 words.
source_label: Ngân hàng đề người dùng cung cấp
source_note: Đọc từ ảnh gốc. Số ước lượng được ghi about/approximately trong bài.

paragraphs.introduction: The diagram illustrates the water cycle, showing how water moves between the ocean, the atmosphere and the land.
paragraphs.overview: Overall, this is a continuous natural cycle involving evaporation, cloud formation and precipitation. Water returns to the ocean through surface and underground routes, after which the cycle can begin again.
paragraphs.body1: First, heat from the sun causes water to evaporate from the ocean and rise into the air as water vapour. The diagram indicates that the ocean contributes about 80% of the water vapour in the air. As this vapour rises, it condenses and forms clouds. These clouds move over the land, where water falls as precipitation, including snow in the higher areas.
paragraphs.body2: After reaching the land, water follows several paths. Some flows over the surface as runoff, and some collects in lakes. Another portion moves below the ground as groundwater. prompt: The pie charts compare the main reasons for immigration to and emigration from the UK in 2007. Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant. Write at least 150 words.

paragraphs.introduction: The pie charts compare the main reasons for immigration to and emigration from the UK in 2007.
paragraphs.overview: Overall, having a definite job was the most common reason in both directions. Formal study was much more important for people entering the UK, while looking for work and giving no stated reason were more common among those leaving.
paragraphs.body1: A definite job accounted for 30% of immigration and a similar 29% of emigration. Formal study was the second largest reason for immigration, at 26%, but represented only 4% of emigration, the smallest share in that chart. Accompanying or joining someone was also slightly more common among arrivals, at 15%, compared with 13% among departures.
paragraphs.body2: By contrast, 22% of people leaving the UK were looking for work, whereas the corresponding figure for immigration was 12%. The share giving no reason was three times as high for emigration, at 18%, as for immigration, at 6%. Other reasons accounted for the remaining 14% of departures and 11% of arrivals. Thus, the two groups differed mainly in the importance of study and job searching, rather than having an existing job.

paragraphs.introduction: The pie charts compare the shares of online retail sales accounted for by four sectors in Canada in 2005 and 2010.
paragraphs.overview: Overall, food and beverages and video games increased their shares, while electronics and appliances and home furnishings declined. Food and beverages replaced electronics and appliances as the largest online retail sector by 2010.
paragraphs.body1: In 2005, electronics and appliances made up 35% of online sales, the highest proportion among the four sectors. Home furnishings ranked second at 25%, followed by food and beverages at 22%. Video games had the smallest share, at 18%. Together, electronics and appliances and home furnishings represented three fifths of the total in that year.
paragraphs.body2: By 2010, the share for food and beverages had risen by ten percentage points to 32%, putting it slightly ahead of electronics and appliances, which fell to 30%. Video games also grew, reaching 23% and moving above home furnishings. The latter category experienced the largest decline, from 25% to 15%, and became the smallest sector. These changes describe the distribution of online sales rather than changes in the total value of sales.

title: World water and water use
prompt: The charts show the distribution of the world’s water and compare water use in Egypt, Saudi Arabia and Canada. Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant. Write at least 150 words.

paragraphs.introduction: The charts show the distribution of the world’s water and compare water use in Egypt, Saudi Arabia and Canada.
paragraphs.overview: Overall, almost all the world’s water is salt water, and most fresh water is stored in ice and glaciers. Agriculture is the main user of water in Egypt and Saudi Arabia, whereas industry dominates water use in Canada.
paragraphs.body1: Salt water accounts for 97% of all water, leaving only 3% as fresh water. Within the fresh-water category, ice and glaciers make up 79%. Groundwater represents a further 20%, while surface water accounts for just 1%. It is important that these last three percentages refer only to fresh water, rather than to the world’s total supply.
paragraphs.body2: The pattern of use differs sharply across the countries. In Egypt, agriculture consumes approximately 80% of water, compared with around 15% for domestic purposes and less than 10% for industry. Saudi Arabia has a similar distribution, with about three quarters used in agriculture and much smaller domestic and industrial shares. Canada shows the opposite pattern: industry takes roughly 80%, while agriculture and domestic use each account for only around a tenth.

prompt: The diagram shows how rainwater and household wastewater are collected, treated and reused in a residential area. Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant. Write at least 150 words.

paragraphs.introduction: The diagram shows how rainwater and household wastewater are collected, treated and reused in a residential area.
paragraphs.overview: Overall, the system uses several routes to manage water. Rainwater is stored in a dam or a household tank, while wastewater is treated for reuse. Excess treated water and stormwater follow separate routes towards the wider water system.
paragraphs.body1: Rain falling in the upper part of the area collects in a dam. Water from the dam passes through a water treatment plant before being supplied to the house as drinking water. Rain falling on the roof is collected separately in a rainwater tank beside the building. This provides another source of water for household use, rather than sending all roof water directly away from the property.
paragraphs.body2: After water has been used in the house, household wastewater flows to a wastewater treatment plant. The diagram shows recycled water returning from this system towards the house, while excess treated water is released along another route. Rainwater flowing over the ground is directed to stormwater treatment before reaching the waterway. Thus, the diagram distinguishes drinking-water treatment, wastewater recycling and the management of surface rainwater.

title: Glass recycling
prompt: The diagram shows how used glass bottles are recycled and returned to customers through supermarkets. Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant. Write at least 150 words.

paragraphs.introduction: The diagram shows how used glass bottles are recycled and returned to customers through supermarkets.
paragraphs.overview: Overall, the process has three main stages, covering collection, cleaning and remanufacturing. Used bottles are cleaned and melted, and the resulting glass is shaped into new bottles before being sent back for sale.
paragraphs.body1: First, empty glass bottles are placed at a collection point. They are collected by a truck and transported to a cleaning plant. At this plant, high-pressure water is used to wash the bottles. The clean glass is then separated into three colour groups: brown, green and clear. These groups are sent on to a recycling plant for the next part of the process.
paragraphs.body2: At the recycling plant, the glass passes through a furnace and becomes recycled liquid glass. New liquid glass is also added before the material goes into a mould. The mould gives the glass the shape of a bottle. In the final stage, the newly formed bottles are supplied to supermarkets for customers. After use, the bottles can return to the collection point and go through the recycling process again.

prompt: The diagram shows how coffee is produced and prepared for sale in shops and supermarkets. Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant. Write at least 150 words.
source_label: Ngân hàng đề người dùng cung cấp
source_note: Đọc từ ảnh gốc. Số ước lượng được ghi about/approximately trong bài.

paragraphs.introduction: The diagram shows how coffee is produced and prepared for sale in shops and supermarkets.
paragraphs.overview: Overall, the process begins with picking coffee beans and ends with packing the finished coffee into jars. Between these stages, the beans are dried and roasted, then processed with water before the mixture is frozen and dried again.
paragraphs.body1: First, coffee beans are picked from the plants and spread out to dry in the sun. The dried beans are then roasted in a machine. After roasting, they are cooled rapidly and ground into smaller pieces. The ground coffee is mixed with hot water, and the mixture is strained to separate the liquid from the remaining solid material.

paragraphs.overview: Overall, urban populations increase in all four countries. The USA has the highest proportion for most of the period, but Korea is expected to reach the same level by 2030. India remains the least urbanised country at the end.
paragraphs.body1: In 1970, approximately 70% of the US population lived in cities, compared with 40% in Korea. paragraphs.body2: China and India both began at about 20%. China remained at this level until 1990, then rose sharply to 50% in 2000 and approximately 60% in 2010. Its figure is projected to reach around 66% in 2030. India increased more slowly, reaching about 30% in 1990 and 35% in 2010, with a further rise to roughly 38% expected by the end.

paragraphs.overview: Overall, science qualifications accounted for the larger share in both years. The proportion with a science PhD increased markedly, while the shares with first degrees in either science or arts declined.
paragraphs.body1: In 1998, first degrees in science were the largest category, at 29%, followed by master’s degrees in science at 25%. paragraphs.body2: By 2008, science PhDs had become the largest category, reaching 30%. Master’s degrees in science increased slightly to 29%, and the share with a master’s degree in arts rose to 13%. Arts PhDs also became more common, at 7%. In contrast, the proportion with a first degree in science fell sharply to 11%, and the figure for first degrees in arts halved to 10%. The workforce therefore had a greater share of postgraduate qualifications in the second year.

title: Energy loss from coal
prompt: The diagrams compare how much energy is lost when electricity is generated from black coal and brown coal, based on an input of 100 units. Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant. Write at least 150 words.
source_label: Ngân hàng đề người dùng cung cấp

paragraphs.introduction: The diagrams compare how much energy is lost when electricity is generated from black coal and brown coal, based on an input of 100 units.
paragraphs.overview: Overall, most energy is lost at the power station in both systems. Black coal delivers more energy to consumers than brown coal, while the loss during transmission and distribution is the same for both.
paragraphs.body1: In the black-coal system, 100 units of fuel energy enter the power station. Of this input, 68 units are lost, leaving 32 units to continue to the transmission and distribution stage. A further three units are lost at that point. As a result, consumers receive 29 units of energy, which is less than one third of the original input.
paragraphs.body2: The brown-coal system follows the same sequence but loses more energy at the first stage. The power station loses 73 out of the initial 100 units, so only 27 units remain. Transmission and distribution then remove another three units, leaving 24 units for consumers. Compared with black coal, brown coal therefore loses five additional units at the power station and delivers five fewer units at the end of the process.

paragraphs.introduction: The table compares the average monthly expenditure of an Australian family on six categories in 1991 and 2001, in Australian dollars.
paragraphs.overview: Overall, total spending increased slightly over the period. Other goods and services remained the largest expense, while electricity and water showed the greatest increase. Clothing and transport were the only categories to decline.
paragraphs.body1: Total monthly expenditure rose from A$675 in 1991 to A$715 in 2001. Other goods and services, defined as non-essential items, increased from A$250 to A$270 and stayed well ahead of every other category. Food was the second largest expense, rising only slightly from A$155 to A$160. Housing also increased by A$5, from A$95 to A$100.
paragraphs.body2: The most noticeable growth was in electricity and water, which rose from A$75 to A$120 per month. This increase moved the category above housing in 2001. By contrast, spending on transport fell from A$70 to A$45, a reduction of A$25. Clothing expenditure also declined, from A$30 to A$20. It remained the smallest item in both years, accounting for much less than any other category.

Macquarie Island had much smaller numbers: 350 visitors initially, followed by 310 in 1998 and a partial recovery to 330 in 2000.

Body 1: bố cục cũ. Body 2: thay đổi hiện tại.
Chép toàn bộ lời đề vào body 1, chỉ đưa ý kiến cá nhân ở body 2.
accepted_answers: Body 1: bố cục cũ. Body 2: thay đổi hiện tại.
quizzes.explanation_vi: Body 1: bố cục cũ. Body 2: thay đổi hiện tại. Cách chia này gom thông tin để so sánh hoặc theo dõi quy trình; không phải cách chia duy nhất hợp lệ.

quizzes.prompt: Sắp xếp hai phần theo câu mẫu. Nhập mã theo thứ tự, ví dụ 2,1.
options: bookshelves were positioned along both the upper and lower sides of the library.
Five years ago,
quizzes.explanation_vi: Câu mẫu: Five years ago, bookshelves were positioned along both the upper and lower sides of the library. Giữ phần mở đầu trước phần bổ sung; đây là bài nhớ câu đã cho.

quizzes.prompt: Hiện tại có bao nhiêu private studying tables ở giữa thư viện?
quizzes.explanation_vi: Đếm2 hàng×3 bàn=6, trước đây4 bàn. The number of tables increased from four to six.

sentence_notes.sentence: Five years ago, bookshelves were positioned along both the upper and lower sides of the library.
sentence_notes.explanation_vi: were là be số nhiều, quá khứ; dùng với số liệu hoặc đối tượng số nhiều.

sentence_notes.sentence: On the left were a classroom, a meeting room and a combined borrowing and returning desk.
sentence_notes.explanation_vi: were là be số nhiều, quá khứ; dùng với số liệu hoặc đối tượng số nhiều.

sentence_notes.sentence: The library office was in the lower-right corner.
sentence_notes.explanation_vi: in dùng trước năm, giai đoạn hoặc địa điểm trong câu này.

sentence_notes.sentence: The lower bookshelves and the former computer desk have been replaced by desks for students’ laptops.
sentence_notes.explanation_vi: by chỉ tác nhân trong bị động hoặc mốc hoàn thành/mức chênh lệch tùy câu.

sentence_notes.sentence: The classroom has become a recording studio, while the meeting room remains in the same position.
sentence_notes.explanation_vi: while nối hai mệnh đề tương phản hoặc hai đặc điểm cần đối chiếu.

checklist_vi: Đúng đối tượng, năm và đơn vị của ảnh.
Overview nêu đặc điểm nổi bật, không suy đoán nguyên nhân.
Body chia nhóm hợp lý và có số liệu/chi tiết hỗ trợ.
Đã kiểm tra thì, số ít/số nhiều và giới từ.
Dùng từ quen thuộc đúng nghĩa; không ép từ đồng nghĩa.
Nếu viết cả bài: ít nhất 150 từ; không có trần chính thức 220 từ.
